items.title: Almost-additive sequences have a normalized limit
items.statement: Let $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a real sequence for which there is a finite constant $K$ with $|a_n|\le Kn$ for every $n\ge1$. Suppose there is a finite constant $C\ge0$ such that $|a_{m+n}-a_m-a_n|\le C$ for all positive integers $m,n$. Then $a_n/n$ has a finite limit as $n\to\infty$.
items.strategy: Shift by ±C to obtain subadditive and superadditive sequences, apply the sourced Fekete limit lemma to each, and use their vanishing normalized gap to conclude.

references.title: Sébastien Gouëzel, Theory Fekete, Archive of Formal Proofs, lemma almost_additive_converges
references.locator: Subsection Almost additive sequences, lemma almost_additive_converges, lines 277–323.

items.title: Finite MDP with bounded real rewards
items.statement: Let $S$ be a finite nonempty state set and let $A(s)$ be a finite nonempty action set for each $s\in S$, as in the finite-MDP convention. Put $D=\{(s,a):s\in S,\ a\in A(s)\}$ with its discrete sigma-algebra. Equip $S$ with its power-set sigma-algebra, $[0,1]$ with its Borel sigma-algebra, and $S\times[0,1]$ with the product sigma-algebra. A finite MDP with bounded real rewards specifies a probability kernel $Q$ from $D$ to $S\times[0,1]$; equivalently, each admissible $(s,a)$ has a probability measure $Q(\cdot\mid s,a)$ on that product measurable space. The reward-coordinate projection $(s',\rho)\mapsto\rho$ is measurable because the preimage of each Borel set $B\subseteq[0,1]$ is the product rectangle $S\times B$. Define the next-state law by $P(s'\mid s,a)=Q(\{s'\}\times[0,1]\mid s,a)$ and the mean reward by $r(s,a)=\int_{S\times[0,1]}\rho\,Q(ds',d\rho\mid s,a)\in[0,1]$. At each time, conditional on the observed history and the selected action, the next-state/reward pair has this law. Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path-space construction under policies.
items.strategy: State the exact finite-state model, conventions, and hypotheses; justify the stated conclusion from the cited interfaces.

items.title: Extended value iteration for a confidence set
items.statement:
Input finite nonempty state and action sets, upper reward estimates $\widetilde r(s,a)$, empirical transition laws $\widehat P(\cdot\mid s,a)$, nonnegative transition radii $b_p(s,a)$, a tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, and fixed orders of the states and actions for tie-breaking. For a vector $v\in\mathbb R^S$, write $\operatorname{span}(v)=\max_s v(s)-\min_s v(s)$ and let $\Delta(S)$ be the probability simplex on $S$. Initialize $u_0(s)=0$. At iteration $i\ge1$, compute
$$u_i(s)=\max_{a\in A(s)}\left[\widetilde r(s,a)+\max_{q\in\Delta(S):\|q-\widehat P(\cdot\mid s,a)\|_1\le b_p(s,a)}q\cdot u_{i-1}\right].$$
For each state, record the first action in the fixed order attaining the outer maximum and a maximizing transition vector $q_i(\cdot\mid s)$; the inner maximum exists because each nonempty feasible subset of $\Delta(S)$ is compact. If $\operatorname{span}(u_i-u_{i-1})<\varepsilon$, return the recorded stationary deterministic policy, maximizing transition vectors, the vector $u_{i-1}$ used in that backup, and the iteration index. A deterministic maximizing transition vector can be computed by moving up to $\min\{1,b_p(s,a)/2\}$ probability mass from the lowest-valued states to a highest-valued state, with the fixed state order resolving equal values; stop moving mass when that state reaches probability one. This finite rule makes the returned quantities measurable functions of the estimates. Otherwise continue. The algorithm is a partial procedure unless a separate termination result is established.

items.title: Communicating MDP and diameter
items.statement: For a finite MDP with bounded rewards, a policy assigns a probability distribution on $A(s)$ to each finite observed history ending in state $s$, with each action probability a measurable function of the history; deterministic policies are included. For states $x,y$, start at $S_0=x$ and define $\tau_y=\inf\{t\ge0:S_t=y\}$. The MDP is communicating if $\inf_\pi\mathbb E_x^\pi[\tau_y]<\infty$ for every ordered pair $(x,y)$. Its raw diameter is $D_0=\max_{x,y}\inf_\pi\mathbb E_x^\pi[\tau_y]$, and its normalized diameter is $D=\max\{1,D_0\}$. Thus a one-state MDP has $D_0=0$ and $D=1$.

items.title: Adaptive MDP visits admit fixed sample tapes
items.statement: Fix a finite-horizon interaction of length $T$ in a finite MDP with bounded rewards and any nonanticipating policy: each action distribution is a measurable function of the revealed history, and policy randomization is independent of unexposed MDP samples. On an enlarged probability space with the same law for the observed interaction, for each admissible pair $(s,a)$ there is a sequence $Z_{s,a,1},\ldots,Z_{s,a,T}$ of independent samples with common law $Q(\cdot\mid s,a)$ such that the $j$th observed next-state/reward pair at $(s,a)$ is $Z_{s,a,j}$ whenever that visit occurs.
items.strategy: Construct a finite product array with the Ionescu–Tulcea kernel theorem and couple adaptive visits by revealing the next unused coordinate for the selected pair.

items.title: Termination of extended value iteration under communicating assumptions
items.statement:
For every finite nonempty state/action system, bounded real upper rewards, probability-vector empirical centers, strictly positive transition radii, and tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, extended value iteration terminates. More precisely, write $F$ for its optimistic Bellman operator, put $\eta=\min_{s,a}\min\{1,b_p(s,a)/2\}>0$, and set $u_0=0$, $u_i=F(u_{i-1})$. Then
$$\operatorname{span}(u_i-u_{i-1})\le(1-\eta)^{i-1}\operatorname{span}(u_1),\qquad i\ge1.$$
When $\eta=1$, the span is zero for $i\ge2$. In particular, the positive UCRL2 confidence radii give finite stopping with tolerance $1/\sqrt{t_k}$ in every episode of a finite communicating MDP, including episodes whose confidence set misses the true model.
items.strategy: Decompose each positive L1 ball into a common positive mass and a residual subprobability; prove a span contraction and geometric decay.

items.title: Uniform empirical reward and transition confidence bounds
items.statement:
Let a finite MDP have $S\ge1$ states and at most $A\ge1$ actions per state, and let $T\ge1$ be an integer and $\delta\in(0,1)$. For each state-action pair $(s,a)$, whenever it has received $n$ visits by time $T$, let $\widehat r_n(s,a)$ be the mean of those first $n$ rewards and let $\widehat P_n(\cdot\mid s,a)$ be the empirical law of those next states. With probability at least $1-\delta$, simultaneously for all such pairs and all $1\le n\le T$,
$$|\widehat r_n(s,a)-r(s,a)|\le\sqrt{\frac{7\log(4SAT/\delta)}{2n}},\qquad \|\widehat P_n(\cdot\mid s,a)-P(\cdot\mid s,a)\|_1\le\sqrt{\frac{14S\log(4AT/\delta)}{n}},$$
where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
items.strategy: Apply Azuma–Hoeffding to fixed tape prefixes, convert transition ℓ1 error to a maximum over subsets, and union over pairs and sample counts.

items.title: Communicating MDPs have a common optimal average reward
items.statement: For a finite communicating MDP with rewards in $[0,1]$, let $V_n(s)$ be the supremum of the expected sum of the first $n$ rewards over all history-dependent policies starting from state $s$. For every state $s$, the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty}V_n(s)/n$ exists, is independent of $s$, and belongs to $[0,1]$.
items.strategy: Bound the finite-horizon value span by the diameter using a target-hitting policy, then show the maximum values are almost additive and invoke the proved normalized-limit lemma.

items.title: UCRL2 for finite communicating MDPs
items.statement:
Input a finite communicating MDP, horizon $T\ge1$, confidence parameter $\delta\in(0,1)$, and fixed orders of states/actions. Start one episode at $t_1=1$. At the start $t_k$ of episode $k$, let $N_k(s,a)$ be the number of visits to $(s,a)$ before $t_k$, with empirical reward mean $\widehat r_k(s,a)=0$ and a fixed default probability vector when $N_k(s,a)=0$. Otherwise use the empirical mean reward and empirical next-state distribution. Put $n_k(s,a)=\max\{1,N_k(s,a)\}$ and
$$b^r_k(s,a)=\sqrt{\frac{7\log(2SAt_k/\delta)}{2n_k(s,a)}},\qquad b^p_k(s,a)=\sqrt{\frac{14S\log(2At_k/\delta)}{n_k(s,a)}}.$$
Set $\widetilde r_k(s,a)=\min\{1,\widehat r_k(s,a)+b^r_k(s,a)\}$. Run extended value iteration with these estimates/radii and tolerance $1/\sqrt{t_k}$, obtaining a stationary deterministic policy $\pi_k$. Let $v_k(s,a)$ start at zero and count visits within this episode. Follow $\pi_k$ until some $v_k(s,a)$ reaches $\max\{1,N_k(s,a)\}$, or until $T$ observations have been made; then start the next episode if time remains. All ties use the fixed orders. The positive radii ensure finite inner termination by the separate termination lemma. In particular, always $v_k(s,a)\le\max\{1,N_k(s,a)\}$; when $N_k(s,a)>0$, a completed triggering episode doubles that pair's total count.

items.title: Average reward and pathwise regret
items.statement: For a finite communicating MDP, let $\rho^*$ denote the common optimal average reward. The existence and independence of this value from the initial state are proved in the immediately cited theorem. Under any policy, write $R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\rho_t$ for the realized cumulative reward over the first $T$ interactions. The pathwise regret is the random variable $\Delta_T=T\rho^*-R_T$. Its expected regret is $\mathbb E[\Delta_T]=T\rho^*-\mathbb E[R_T]$. The pathwise random variable and its expectation are distinct objects.

items.title: UCRL2 high-probability pathwise regret bound
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path-law and martingale suppliers. Let a finite communicating MDP have $S\ge1$ states, at most $A\ge1$ actions per state, rewards in $[0,1]$, and normalized diameter $D$. For each initial state, integer horizon $T\ge2$, and $\delta\in(0,1)$, UCRL2 with confidence parameter $\delta$ satisfies
$$\Pr\!\left(\Delta_T\le34DS\sqrt{AT\log(T/\delta)}\right)\ge1-\delta.$$
For every integer $T\ge1$, the same algorithm also satisfies
$$\Pr\!\left(\Delta_T\le34DS\sqrt{AT\log(2T/\delta)}\right)\ge1-\delta.$$
Here $\Delta_T=T\rho^*-R_T$ is realized, pathwise regret and logarithms are natural. These are assertions for each fixed horizon and initial state. The original formula with $\log(T/\delta)$ and $T\ge1$ is false, as refuted below.
items.strategy: Use fixed-tape anytime confidence, the local EVI contraction, finite-horizon span control, predictable martingale increments, count doubling, and explicit constants; refute the exact original T=1 formula.

items.title: Expected regret lower bound for communicating MDPs
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited by the probability and Pinsker suppliers. For all integers $S,A\ge10$, all real $D\ge\max\{1,20\log_A S\}$, all integers $T\ge DSA$, every learning algorithm, and every prescribed initial state label, there exists a finite communicating MDP with exactly $S$ states including that label, exactly $A$ actions in each state, rewards in $[0,1]$, and normalized diameter at most $D$, such that the algorithm's expected regret from that initial state satisfies
$$\mathbb E[T\rho^*-R_T]\ge0.015\sqrt{DSAT}.$$
The MDP may depend on the algorithm, parameters, and prescribed initial state. The original planned statement with reversed minimax quantifiers and no feasibility condition $D\ge1$ is false; it is retained and refuted below.
items.strategy: Prove the corrected minimax constant by an exact-state/action two-state-pair tree and separate small-diameter bandit construction, with finite-history KL/Pinsker and complete constant transfer; refute original infeasible scope.

items.title: A noncommunicating MDP can have state-dependent average reward
items.statement: Let $S=\{0,1\}$ and let each state have one action. Both states are absorbing. The reward is always $0$ in state $0$ and always $1$ in state $1$. The MDP is not communicating, and its long-run average reward is $0$ from initial state $0$ and $1$ from initial state $1$.

items.title: One-state MDP and normalized diameter
items.statement: Let $S=\{s\}$, $A(s)=\{a\}$, let the transition return to $s$ with probability one, and let every reward equal $1$. Then the MDP is communicating, its raw diameter is $D_0=0$, its normalized diameter is $D=1$, its optimal average reward is $1$, and its unique policy has regret $0$ at every horizon.

items.title: A random reward separates pathwise and expected regret
items.statement: Let there be one state and one action, with deterministic self-transition and independent Bernoulli$(1/2)$ rewards. Then $\rho^*=1/2$. At horizon $T=1$, pathwise regret equals $1/2$ when the reward is $0$ and equals $-1/2$ when the reward is $1$, although expected regret is $0$.
